records.title: Nested Format String Support with Recursive Parsing
records.body:
Cannot parse nested structures like `"outer: {inner: {value:d}}"

> Feature Request

Support nested format strings: `parse("{level1: {level2: {level3:d}}}", string)`
Implement recursive parser that tracks nesting depth
Handle escaped braces at any nesting level
Support mixing named and positional args in nested structures
Add `max_nesting_depth` parameter (default 10) to prevent stack overflow

Test Complexity
5+ levels of nesting
Mixed named/positional at different levels
Escaped braces within nested structures
Malformed nesting (unclosed braces at various depths)
Circular reference detection

Why Complex
Recursive regex generation
State tracking for multiple nesting levels
Ambiguity resolution (which closing brace matches which opening)
Memory management for deep recursion

records.title: Possibility to use Recursive function?
records.body:
Hello,
I am currently evaluating APIs to use with our setup and yours really comes close.
However, I am using a few recursive functions in postgreSQL, a function looks like this:

```
CREATE FUNCTION recursive_geo(integer[]) RETURNS TABLE(id integer, parent_id integer)
    LANGUAGE sql
    AS $_$
WITH RECURSIVE included_geo(iid, iparent) AS (
    SELECT id, parent FROM geo WHERE id = ANY($1)
  UNION ALL
    SELECT p.id, p.parent
    FROM included_geo pr, geo p
    WHERE p.parent = pr.iid
  )
SELECT iid, iparent
FROM included_geo;
$_$;

```
Which I then call like this:
`select id as hasid from recursive_geo(${data.all.geo})
`
where _data.all.geo_ is the parameter passed to the query
is it possible to do this with RestSQL?
Could I f.e. just declare "recursive_geo" as a table? (It is actually a temporary table after all)

Thanks a lot in advance for any help!

I'm currently working on fixing some code splitting ordering issues in esbuild (https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/399) and I noticed that Rollup has a similar problem. Here's an example problem case:

```js
// main.js
import './lib2'
import './lib1'
if (window.lib !== 'lib1') throw 'fail'
```

```js
// main2.js
import './lib1'
import './lib2'
if (window.lib !== 'lib2') throw 'fail'
```

```js
// lib1.js
window.lib = 'lib1'
```

```js
// lib2.js
window.lib = 'lib2'
```

I have a way to solve this in esbuild but it's a pretty big rewrite. Solving this is potentially a step up in complexity, so it's understandable why Rollup hasn't tackled this yet.

I figured I should log this in case it's not already a known issue. I did a quick search and the best I found was https://github.com/rollup/rollup/issues/3356, but it doesn't seem like this exact issue is covered by that one. My apologies if this issue is already known. If that's the case, feel free to close this.

### Expected Behavior

Both generated entry point chunks respect the correct module execution order and don't throw.

### Actual Behavior

One of the generated entry point chunks that Rollup generates will throw because common code that is shared between both of the entry points is evaluated in the wrong order. It's easy to see why this happens from the generated code:

```js
// output/main.js
import './lib1-4ba6e17e.js';
if (window.lib !== 'lib1') throw 'fail'
```

```js
// output/main2.js
import './lib1-4ba6e17e.js';
if (window.lib !== 'lib2') throw 'fail'
```

```js
// output/lib1-4ba6e17e.js
window.lib = 'lib2';
window.lib = 'lib1';
```

Memory usage with recursive file list
records.body:
When using "s3cmd ls --recursive" on a path with a huge number of files (for example, 1 million files), the process seems to fetch all the data into memory before writing to stdout. This is works well until the oom-killer kills the process due to excessive memory consumption.

Would it be possible to add a new option to write the list directly stdout after each API request is completed?

records.title: With Recursive query results in "no relation" error with SQLite
records.body:
### Version

1.27.0

### What happened?

WIth Recursive query fails to recognize the relation in SQLite when I run `sqlc generate`. 

not sure if this works with SQLite, but I tried adding this to config, but it didn't work.
```yaml
datebase:
    managed: true
```
I'm aware of #723 and #896, and it seems the fix only applies to PostgreSQL + MySQL. But perhaps this bug is more relevant with #2990 even though it happens with MySQL instead.

### Relevant log output

```shell
# package db
query.sql:1:1: relation "TagWithParents" does not exist
```


### Database schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE tags (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    parent INTEGER NOT NULL
);
```


### SQL queries

```sql
-- name: GetTagRecursive :many
WITH RECURSIVE TagWithParents AS (
    SELECT id, name, parent
    FROM tags
    WHERE id = ?

    UNION ALL

    SELECT t.id, t.name, t.parent
    FROM tags t
    INNER JOIN TagWithParents twp
    ON t.id = twp.parent
) SELECT * FROM TagWithParents;
```


### Configuration

```yaml
version: "2" 

sql: 
  - engine: "sqlite" 
    queries: "query.sql" 
    schema: "schema.sql" 
    gen: 
      go: 
        package: "db" 
        out: "db"
```


### Playground URL

https://play.sqlc.dev/p/bebb509cacaeae9488c4c5c08f9f554d35375fe581dc0c477286ac2bb87a4bcc

### What operating system are you using?

Linux

### What database engines are you using?

SQLite

### What type of code are you generating?

Go
